Let \(A\) be the origin. Set
\[
\mathbf u=\overrightarrow{AB},\qquad \mathbf v=\overrightarrow{AC},
\]
so \(|\mathbf u|=11\) and \(|\mathbf v|=13\). Let \(\mathbf o\) be the position vector of \(O\), and
\[
\mathbf g=\frac{\mathbf u+\mathbf v}{3}
\]
be the position vector of the centroid \(G\). Let \(\mathbf x\) be the position vector of the orthocenter of \(\triangle AGO\).

Since \(O\) is the circumcenter of \(\triangle ABC\),
\[
|\mathbf o|^2=|\mathbf o-\mathbf u|^2 \implies \mathbf o\cdot \mathbf u=\frac{121}{2},
\]
and similarly
\[
\mathbf o\cdot \mathbf v=\frac{169}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbf g\cdot \mathbf o
=\frac13(\mathbf u+\mathbf v)\cdot \mathbf o
=\frac13\left(\frac{121}{2}+\frac{169}{2}\right)
=\frac{145}{3}.
\]

In \(\triangle AGO\), the altitudes from \(G\) and \(O\) give
\[
\mathbf x\cdot \mathbf o=\mathbf g\cdot \mathbf o
\]
and
\[
\mathbf x\cdot \mathbf g=\mathbf g\cdot \mathbf o.
\]
So
\[
\mathbf x\cdot \mathbf o=\frac{145}{3},\qquad \mathbf x\cdot \mathbf g=\frac{145}{3}.
\]

Because the orthocenter lies on line \(BC\), for some real \(t\),
\[
\mathbf x=(1-t)\mathbf u+t\mathbf v.
\]
Using \(\mathbf x\cdot \mathbf o=\frac{145}{3}\),
\[
(1-t)\frac{121}{2}+t\frac{169}{2}=\frac{145}{3}.
\]
So
\[
121+48t=\frac{290}{3}
\implies 48t=-\frac{73}{3}
\implies t=-\frac{73}{144}.
\]

Now let \(d=\mathbf u\cdot \mathbf v\). Using \(\mathbf x\cdot \mathbf g=\frac{145}{3}\),
\[
\left((1-t)\mathbf u+t\mathbf v\right)\cdot \frac{\mathbf u+\mathbf v}{3}
=\frac{145}{3}.
\]
Expanding,
\[
\frac{(1-t)(121+d)+t(d+169)}{3}=\frac{145}{3},
\]
so
\[
121+d+48t=145.
\]
Substitute \(t=-\frac{73}{144}\):
\[
121+d-\frac{73}{3}=145
\]
\[
d=24+\frac{73}{3}=\frac{145}{3}.
\]

Finally,
\[
BC^2=|\mathbf v-\mathbf u|^2
=|\mathbf v|^2+|\mathbf u|^2-2\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v
=169+121-2\cdot\frac{145}{3}
=\frac{580}{3}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
BC=\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}=\frac{2\sqrt{435}}{3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{435}}{3}}
\]
